source_note: All register references are Regione Piemonte's 'Alberi Monumentali del Piemonte: dati del censimento' (CC BY 4.0), read live from the WFS at gisserver.territorio.csi.it. That layer carries an age band, ownership and a removal status per tree. MASAF's national file repeats the same coordinates and girths for Turin, so it is the same survey and not an independent source. Place names come from Turismo Torino's 13.9 km urban route and from the Quotidiano Piemontese and Mole24 lists.

leads.name: The Plane of Parco della Tesoriera
leads.reason: The widest trunk and the tree most often called Turin's oldest, nicknamed the grandfather, but it stands 3.6 km west of this walk in its own park and forms a cluster of one. It is the obvious ninth entry if Turin ever grows past this walk, and it is what the page's oldest-tree question has to name honestly.

leads.name: The Populus nigra of via Don Lorenzo Milani
leads.reason: New find, 2026-08-31 pass, not previously recorded. 6.7 km from centre, girth 5.4 m despite an age band under 100 years, so a fast-growing giant rather than an ancient tree; potentially visually spectacular on size alone. Reverse-geocodes to via Don Lorenzo Milani, Ricovero, Collegno, a separate comune west of Torino, not the city itself. One targeted search ("pioppo nero monumentale Collegno") found the Comune di Collegno's own municipal tree census page exists but returned no specific hit for this tree, and no press coverage. No second source, no place name, no confirmed park/access context, and it would need its own day-trip justification (transit time from Torino centre) rather than joining this walk. Worth a look next pass with a direct fetch of Collegno's tree census, not chased further this pass.

leads.name: The Caucasian Elm of the Giardini Reali Inferiori
leads.reason: Designated for botanical rarity and standing in the Royal Gardens beside the Palazzo Reale, which is a strong setting. Cut only on geometry: it sits 1.05 km north of the Giardini Cavour, the wrong way from a walk that runs south to the river, and adding it would bend a straight line into a Y. Register gives 24 m, the tourist route gives 27 m, so the height needs settling before it ships.

leads.name: [BLOCKED 2026-08-23] The Plane of Parco di Villa Rey
leads.reason: 2.4 km northeast of the walk, up on the hill across the Po. Register height 27 m against the tourist route's 33.5 m, a 6.5 m disagreement that needs a third source. A candidate for a second Turin cluster on the collina, not for this one. BLOCKED 2026-08-23: Villa Rey has been the national headquarters of ASI (Automotoclub Storico Italiano) since 2006, and press coverage of its FAI and Open House Torino open days ('apertura straordinaria', 'non sembra avere orari di apertura permanenti al pubblico') confirms the grounds are not otherwise open; visits require a scheduled public event or an appointment for a specific exhibition. Register 'Pubblica' ownership means the city owns the building, not that the grounds are walk-in accessible. Fails hard rule 10's first test (can a visitor get in without asking anyone's permission). Would need a source stating the plaza itself sits on an unrestricted public path before this could ship.

leads.name: The wide plane east of the Po
leads.reason: Second widest trunk in the city at 6.4 m and yet only 14 m tall, which almost certainly means a pollarded or topped tree. Neither the tourist route nor either press list names it, so it has no place name at all yet and no second source. Worth a look because of the girth, but the height ratio needs explaining before it could be written. CHECKED 2026-08-23: this is NOT the press-documented 'plane of Corso Novara by the Cimitero Monumentale' (see that separate, already-blocked lead below); this point sits about 1.8km further southeast, on the Sassi hillside. A reverse geocode of the coordinate returns 'Villa Rey' as the nearest named OSM feature, roughly 250m off, which may just be sparse tagging on that hillside rather than evidence the tree stands on Villa Rey's own grounds (Villa Rey's registered plane, reg_id 009, is a separate point 1.8km away and is itself blocked on access, see above). Still no name, no second source and no confirmed access status. Do not ship without a real site identification; worth a look at Google Street View or a Sassi/Madonna del Pilone neighbourhood association page next pass. CHECKED AGAIN 2026-08-31: Nominatim reverse geocode places the exact point at 92 int. 119, Corso Quintino Sella, Madonna del Pilone, within Torino proper (Circoscrizione 7, Sassi). Three separate searches this pass (platano + Madonna del Pilone/Sassi/Corso Quintino Sella; platano + Sassi/collina Po/censimento; platano + Villa Rey/Borgata Sassi) and one attempted fetch of the torinocronaca.it 16-monumental-trees survey and the 5wagora.com monumental-trees article (both loaded fine and list all 16 named register trees by park) found this tree in neither: it genuinely has no press coverage and no place name anywhere found, confirming the 2026-08-23 finding rather than overturning it. Register remains the sole source. Still a lead, not shippable without a second source under BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's two-source bar.

leads.name: The three oaks of the Borgo Medievale, if they are ever split
leads.reason: Blocked as shipped (see below) because the register files them as one GRUPPO with no measurements. Kept as a lead because the press lists them individually at 27 m each, so if a municipal source ever gives them separate girths and points, they are three ready-made entries sitting in the middle of a walk that already passes them. [SKIPPED 2026-09-01 by the write pass: rather than a tree, this is a register GRUPPO with no per-tree measurements and no split confirmed; not a collectible point as things stand. worth a later pass only if a municipal source ever splits it into three dated, measured entries.]

blocked.name: Group of oaks at the Borgo Medievale
blocked.reason: Register type GRUPPO with no girth, height, age or crown recorded, so there is no one identifiable tree to stand in front of and nothing to verify per trunk.

blocked.name: Group of oaks near Superga
blocked.reason: Register type GRUPPO with no measurements, and 5.6 km from the centre. Not a collectible point.

blocked.name: Double avenue of planes, southwest of the city
blocked.reason: Register type FILARE DOPPIO, a double avenue rather than a tree, and privately owned. Fails the collectible-point test and hard rule 10 at once.

blocked.name: Avenue of oaks, northwest of the city
blocked.reason: Register type VIALE ALBERATO, an avenue. Nothing to stand at and nothing to have seen.

blocked.name: The plane of Corso Novara, by the Cimitero Monumentale
blocked.register_id: not present in the current regional layer
blocked.reason: Named by Turismo Torino's route and both press lists at 27 m, but absent from the regional census layer as read on 2026-08-05, and the council has run an active felling programme on Corso Novara for trees at risk of falling. Vitality unconfirmed on a street where trees are being taken down. Do not publish without a current municipal source saying this individual still stands.

blocked.name: Oak on private land, northeast of the city
blocked.reason: Register ownership Privata. Private land with no evidence it is open to visitors.

blocked.name: Holm oak on private land, south of the city
blocked.reason: Register ownership Privata, and the age field reads 'Non applicabile'. Private land, no public access recorded.

blocked.name: Service tree on private land, southeast of the city
blocked.reason: Register ownership Privata. Also only 133 cm round, well under anything this site would call remarkable.
